brief: Memory pricing keeps rising and hyperscalers are absorbing the cost rather than cutting orders: Amazon attributed part of its latest capex increase to higher memory prices, which the note reads as a signal that memory suppliers retain pricing power. Despite that, memory equities have not kept pace, consolidating for weeks. The DRAM ETF sits squeezed between a rising trend line from launch and a falling trend line from its highs, with price back above its 21-day moving average; a break higher from this consolidation could get aggressive quickly. Among components, Micron shows the better relative momentum, having closed back above its 50-day moving average, with a proper close above $1,000 flagged as a potential squeeze trigger. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix remain pinned near major support, both squeezed between a bigger positive trend and a shorter-term negative trend, with Hynix's 50-day average still well above current price. Korean retail speculation has cooled off massively and KOSPI volatility has been crushed, so the note flags KOSPI upside convexity as one way to play a possible catch-up squeeze in memory stocks.
